result.instructions: Records GPU use on Apple silicon with Metal System Trace. A metal-gpu-trace.json in the repository gives each project its own recordings folder; project_info says which project is active. One recording runs at a time; keep other GPU work off the Mac while it records, and keep the program's window visible: a hidden window stops presenting, and the work after that is left out of the frames (gpu.unpresented; perf_gate fails such a run). Under Wine record 30 s or more: Wine's start-up takes part of the recording. A recording needs about 0.8 GB of free disk per second for Instruments' temporary files (26 GB for 30 s, 50 GB for 60 s); perf_record refuses to start without it. Reading a recording back takes 1 to 14 s per recorded second. Compare only recordings with 100 frames or more, and repeat a run before calling a change real. perf_baseline (or perf_baseline_record, which records them) saves several equal runs as a named reference and perf_check says whether a new run regressed against their range. perf_diagnose says whether a run splits its GPU work into too many short encoders, as translation layers do; perf_compare says how much two runs differ; skip_s on perf_compare, perf_gate and perf_panel leaves out the first seconds (start-up) of each run; perf_history follows FPS, hitches and memory across runs with one name prefix, oldest first; perf_gate says whether a run meets budgets you set (FPS floor, hitch or memory ceiling); perf_panel writes an HTML page to look at one or two runs in a browser. trace_tables and trace_query need the .trace, kept only with KEEP_TRACE=1. When perf_record ends it stops every program of its Wine prefix, or every process named like a native program. To compare native Metal with a translation layer without a game of one's own: workload_list, workload_fetch, then perf_record with workload and api (and example, for a workload that lists examples), or the compare-layer prompt. perf_sweep records one run per value of dim, example, api or an environment variable and fits GPU ms per frame on the value. memory_free_pct holds the whole Mac short of memory while recording (keep other work off it) and background throttles the program: repeat a run that uses either.

tools.description:
Records `program` (an .exe under Wine, or a macOS binary with wine="native"), or a test program fetched with
workload_fetch (workload, api, dim), for `seconds` with Metal System Trace and returns its summary: GPU ms per
frame, frame intervals, FPS, Metal and resident memory (memory=false skips the Metal memory table, the slowest
to read). When it ends it stops every program of that Wine prefix (wineserver -k), or every process named like
the program with native. counters=true also records Metal GPU Counters (`gpu_counters` in the summary: the units the
GPU waited on, its utilization, occupancy and memory bandwidth); it adds about 40 s of read-back per recorded second.

api.description: with workload: mtl (native Metal), mtl-x64 (Metal built for x86_64, run under Rosetta like Wine), vk (Vulkan through MoltenVK: set METAL_TRACE_MOLTENVK), d3d11 or d3d12 (under wine)

background.description: macOS only, default false; true runs the program under taskpolicy -b, which throttles it hard and unevenly (drawstress: 18 to 280 times slower): repeat the run

counters.description: default false; true also records Metal GPU Counters (gpu_counters in the summary); not under Windows; adds about 40 s of read-back per recorded second

dim.description: with workload drawstress: side of the cube grid, dim^3 draws per frame

env.description: NAME=VALUE pairs separated by spaces, set in the program's environment; MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1 or MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 adds `validation` to the summary: the layers' messages counted by kind

example.description: with a workload that lists examples in workload_list: the one to run

label.description: name for the run: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'

memory.description: default true; false skips the Metal memory table, the slowest to read (about 40 % faster summary): no metal_mib_peak

memory_free_pct.description: macOS only, 20 to 60: holds the whole Mac at this percentage of RAM free while recording (memory_pressure), to see how the program behaves short of memory; lower can freeze the Mac

prefix.description: Wine prefix, default WINEPREFIX or ~/.wine; ignored with native

tools.description:
Records the same program once per value of one variable (dim, example, api, size, or env:NAME for an environment
variable) and returns, per value, the median of FPS, 1 % low, GPU ms per frame and stutter, and with 3 or more
numeric values the straight line GPU ms per frame follows (fixed ms plus ms per draw for dim, per unit otherwise)
with its r2. With rounds above 1 the values run in opposite order every other round, so drift hits all alike.
Runs are named `name`-<value number>-r<round>; each takes its seconds plus about a minute to read back.

tools.title: Record a run twice to find first-seen shader stutter

tools.description:
Records a program that is already running, by pid or by a name in its command line (Game.exe under Wine),
for `seconds` and returns the same summary as perf_record; the program keeps running. For games started by
Steam, CrossOver, NotProton or any launcher: start the game or its benchmark there first.

label.description: name for the run: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'

process.description: pid, or a name in the program's command line such as Game.exe

seconds.description: recording length, default 20; the export afterwards takes several minutes under Wine

tools.name: perf_attach
tools.title: Record a running program

tools.description:
Says which project is active: its name, profile, baseline and format, the folder its recordings go to and
where that folder comes from (the project file, METAL_TRACE_OUT or the default ./perf-runs). Without a project
file, project and baseline are null and profile is generic.
tools.name: project_info
tools.title: Show the active project

tools.description:
Lists the saved recordings, newest first, with frames, FPS, GPU ms per frame, memory peaks and the translation
layer each ran on (fingerprint and Wine, or native); project names the project they belong to (null without a
metal-gpu-trace.json, see project_info).

limit.description: rows per page, default 50, at most 500

tools.name: perf_runs
tools.title: List recordings

tools.description:
Compares two saved recordings (names from perf_runs), a the reference and b the run after a change: the
headline numbers (FPS, GPU ms, frame pacing, memory), then what changed in the GPU work and where: encoders and
command buffers per frame, the share of encoders under short_us, the GPU's idle time, and each encoder label's
count and GPU ms per frame, largest change first. layer says whether both ran on the same translation layer:
with different layers it compares layers, not one change. A Windows run against a Metal run has `measure`: the
GPU ms and Metal memory differ in kind and the encoders exist only in Metal, so use FPS, its lows, stutter and
jitter. Recordings with under 100 frames are flagged: too short to compare. With markdown true the result also has
`markdown`: the same numbers as tables for a PR comment. skip_s leaves out the first seconds of each recording,
where shaders compile and resources load: the GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed from the
per-frame files without them, and `skipped_s` says it; thermal state, process memory and encoders stay whole-run.
`screen` appears when one run was recorded with the screen locked and the other not: FPS is then not comparable.

a.description: run name from perf_runs: the reference, such as the run before a change

b.description: run name from perf_runs: the run to compare against a

markdown.description: also return the numbers as Markdown tables, default false

short_us.description: an encoder under this GPU time counts as short: 10, 25 (default), 50, 100, 250, 500 or 1000

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them

tools.name: perf_compare
tools.title: Compare two recordings

tools.description:
Names a reference for perf_check, or lists them. With name and runs (names from perf_runs, several runs of the
same program recorded with no change between them), it saves copies of their summaries as the reference `name`,
replacing a previous one, and returns the range each number spans across them: that range, not one run, is what
perf_check judges against, since repeated runs differ by a few percent, and `spread_pct`, each range's width in %
of its midpoint: the noise of this program on this machine, which a change must exceed. With name alone it shows that reference;
with nothing it lists them. With skip_s the reference keeps each run without its first skip_s seconds (the
start-up, as perf_compare's skip_s) and perf_check applies the same cut to the run it judges, so both are
steady-state; the runs need their per-frame files for that.

name.description: reference name: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'; alone, shows that reference

runs.description: run names from perf_runs to save as this reference, ideally 3 or more equal runs; replaces a previous one

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them; perf_check applies the same cut to the run it judges

tools.name: perf_baseline
tools.title: Name a reference

annotations.title: Check a run against a reference

tools.description:
Judges a recording against a reference saved with perf_baseline: regressed when FPS falls under the
reference's lowest FPS by more than margin_pct, GPU ms per frame rises over its highest by more than margin_pct,
or encoders or command buffers per frame exceed its highest; improved when a number leaves the range the other
way and none regressed; same otherwise. Frame pacing, short encoders and GPU idle time are reported by the
comparison but do not decide: they vary too much between equal runs. A run from Windows against a Metal
reference (or the reverse) is judged on FPS alone. A reference saved with skip_s judges the run without its first
skip_s seconds too (`skipped_s` says so). Returns the reasons and perf_compare's
full comparison against the reference's first run.

margin_pct.description: how far outside the reference's range FPS or GPU ms per frame may fall before counting, default 3

tools.name: perf_check
tools.title: Check a run against a reference

tools.description:
Writes a recording's GPU frames as a Chrome trace file, `<run>.chrome-trace` in the runs directory, that
ui.perfetto.dev and chrome://tracing open: one slice per GPU frame, from its start for its GPU time (the sum of
its encoders' time, so a frame with parallel encoders can show shorter than it took), with the compute, fragment
and vertex split as arguments. Returns the file name and the number of frames.
tools.name: perf_export_trace
tools.title: Export frames to Perfetto

tools.description:
Checks a recording against budgets and says pass or fail: a floor for FPS and the 1% low, a ceiling for the
stutter rate, the p95 GPU ms per frame, the hitch count and the peak Metal MiB. Give at least one. A number the
recording lacks fails its budget (value null): a gate must not pass on missing data, nor on a recording whose
program stopped presenting (`unpresented`). Returns each budget with its
limit, the value and whether it held. Use it as a bar a change must clear, where perf_check judges against equal runs.
skip_s leaves out the first seconds of the recording (the start-up), as perf_compare does.

fps_1pct_low_min.description: the 1% low FPS must be at least this

fps_min.description: the FPS must be at least this

gpu_ms_p95_max.description: the p95 GPU ms per frame at most this

hitches_max.description: the number of hitches at most this

metal_mib_max.description: the peak Metal memory in MiB at most this

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them

stutter_rate_pct_max.description: the share of stutter frames, in %, at most this

tools.name: perf_gate
tools.title: Check a run against budgets

tools.description:
Lists the recordings whose name starts with `prefix`, oldest first, with their FPS, 1% low, GPU ms, stutter,
hitches and peak Metal MiB, and the change from the first to the last: how a number moved over a series of runs, such as
one recording per version of a translation layer. Read a trend as real only when it exceeds the spread_pct that
perf_baseline reports for equal runs. Runs from Windows and Metal in one series are flagged: their GPU ms and
memory do not compare. skip_s leaves out the first seconds of each recording (the start-up), as perf_compare does.

prefix.description: the start of the run names to follow: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them

tools.name: perf_history
tools.title: Follow a number across runs

tools.description:
Writes one HTML file, `<name>.panel.html` in the runs directory, that shows one or two recordings in a
browser without a server: GPU time per frame with the hitches marked, the numbers (FPS and its lows, frame
time, jitter, stutter, memory, thermal state), Metal memory over time and, for two runs, A against B. The file
holds the data itself, no path, and loads nothing from the network; the viewer can hide and reorder the
widgets and export the layout as JSON. preset `fps` is the timeline, numbers and memory; `compare` (two runs)
puts A against B first. skip_s leaves out the first seconds of each recording (the start-up), as perf_compare does.
layout (tab ids in the order to show) is saved as panel.json in the runs directory and becomes the default tab
order of every panel, the live one too, until the viewer changes it in the browser; ids left out are hidden but
can be switched back on; tabs are tests (each run against the project's reference), summary, ab, frames, encoders, counters,
memory and data (a panel.json that does not name tests shows it first; one that leaves out any other keeps it hidden),
and a panel.json you wrote yourself, or copied from the panel's Layout JSON, works the same.
Returns the file name, the runs, the frames shown and the file's bytes.

layout.description: tabs to show, in order: tests, summary, ab, frames, encoders, counters, memory, data; saved as panel.json in the runs directory as the default for every panel

name.description: name for the panel file: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'

runs.description: one or two run names from perf_runs; with two, the first is A, the reference

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them

tools.name: perf_panel
tools.title: Write an HTML panel

tools.description:
Says whether a saved recording splits its GPU work into too many short encoders, the pattern of translation
layers such as DXMT, Mullion or MoltenVK, with the numbers behind it: encoders and command buffers per frame, the
share of short encoders, the labels with the most GPU time and the GPU's idle time. Read the idle time together
with the FPS: a program waiting for vsync idles too. Defaults come from bgfx 17-drawstress on an M1 Pro: 7
encoders per frame and 50% under 25 us under Mullion, 2 and 2% in native Metal.

min_encoders.description: encoders per frame (median) from which the verdict can be yes, default 4

short_share.description: share of short encoders from which the verdict is yes, default 0.25

short_us.description: an encoder under this GPU time counts as short: 10, 25 (default), 50, 100, 250, 500 or 1000

tools.name: perf_diagnose
tools.title: Diagnose encoder use

tools.description: Lists the data tables (schemas) a .trace recording holds; recordings keep their .trace only with KEEP_TRACE=1.

trace.description: a run name from perf_runs whose trace_kept is true, or the path of a .trace

tools.name: trace_tables
tools.title: List a trace's tables

tools.description:
Counts the rows of several tables of a kept .trace, in all and per process, so a recording's useful tables
show before reading them: a table with 0 rows needs another instrument or Xcode, not a bigger page.

tables.description: table names from trace_tables; default the tables that matter for a translation layer

trace.description: a run name from perf_runs whose trace_kept is true, or the path of a .trace

tools.name: trace_count
tools.title: Count a trace's rows

tools.description: Returns one page of rows of one table of a .trace as {column: value}, optionally only one process's rows.

limit.description: rows per page, default 50, at most 500

schema.description: a table name that trace_tables lists, such as metal-gpu-intervals

trace.description: a run name from perf_runs whose trace_kept is true, or the path of a .trace

tools.name: trace_query

content.text:
Compare drawstress in native Metal with drawstress through d3d12 under the Wine in METAL_TRACE_WINE, with the metal-trace tools:
1. workload_fetch name=drawstress (it is skipped when already downloaded).
2. perf_record label=drawstress-mtl workload=drawstress api=mtl seconds=20.
3. perf_record label=drawstress-d3d12 workload=drawstress api=d3d12 seconds=30.
4. perf_compare a=<the mtl run> b=<the other run>, and perf_diagnose on the other run for its verdict.
Report perf_compare's metrics and encoders as one table (a, b, change), then its labels with the largest change in GPU ms per frame, then the verdict. Say which runs are in too_short, and that one pair of runs is not enough to call a difference real: repeat both before concluding.

{"family": "Apple9", "mac_chips": ["M3 series", "M4 series"], "other_chips": ["A17 Pro", "A18"], "adds": ["full 64-bit atomics", "BC pixel formats on every device", "mesh draws in indirect command buffers", "indirect mesh draw arguments", "ICB memory barriers for rendering", "row-major matrices in acceleration structures", "per-component motion in ray tracing", "MetalFX denoised upscaling", "Dynamic Caching (registers allocated as the program runs)"], "limits": {"mesh_grid_threadgroups": 1048575, "argument_buffer_samplers_per_stage": 500000, "mesh_payload_and_geometry_per_draw": "not stated", "texture_2d_px": 16384}, "same_on_all": {"threads_per_threadgroup": 1024, "threadgroup_memory_bytes": 32768, "mesh_pipeline_payload_bytes": 16384, "argument_buffer_textures_or_buffers_per_stage": 1000000}, "footnotes": ["64-bit atomics: none on Apple7; Apple8 has only ulong min/max, only on macOS; the full set starts with Apple9.", "Mesh draws in indirect command buffers start with Apple9; earlier families refuse such mesh pipelines.", "Inline constexpr samplers count toward the argument buffer sampler limit.", "Mesh shaders on Apple7 and Apple8 can use up to 4 GB of payload and mesh geometry per draw.", "Function pointers and ray tracing in render pipelines are not compatible with mesh shading."], "guards": {"M1 only": "Apple7 && !Apple8", "before M3": "!Apple9"}, "sources": {"families": "https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlgpufamily", "feature_set_tables": "https://developer.apple.com/metal/Metal-Feature-Set-Tables.pdf", "feature_set_tables_date": "2026-05-21", "m3_tech_talk": "https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111375/"}}

adds: BC pixel formats on every device
mesh draws in indirect command buffers
Dynamic Caching (registers allocated as the program runs)
footnotes: 64-bit atomics: none on Apple7; Apple8 has only ulong min/max, only on macOS; the full set starts with Apple9.
Mesh draws in indirect command buffers start with Apple9; earlier families refuse such mesh pipelines.
Inline constexpr samplers count toward the argument buffer sampler limit.
Mesh shaders on Apple7 and Apple8 can use up to 4 GB of payload and mesh geometry per draw.
Function pointers and ray tracing in render pipelines are not compatible with mesh shading.

result.instructions: Records GPU use on Apple silicon with Metal System Trace. A metal-gpu-trace.json in the repository gives each project its own recordings folder; project_info says which project is active. One recording runs at a time; keep other GPU work off the Mac while it records, and keep the program's window visible: a hidden window stops presenting, and the work after that is left out of the frames (gpu.unpresented; perf_gate fails such a run). Under Wine record 30 s or more: Wine's start-up takes part of the recording. A recording needs about 0.8 GB of free disk per second for Instruments' temporary files (26 GB for 30 s, 50 GB for 60 s); perf_record refuses to start without it. Reading a recording back takes 1 to 14 s per recorded second. Compare only recordings with 100 frames or more, and repeat a run before calling a change real. perf_baseline (or perf_baseline_record, which records them) saves several equal runs as a named reference and perf_check says whether a new run regressed against their range. perf_diagnose says whether a run splits its GPU work into too many short encoders, as translation layers do; perf_compare says how much two runs differ; skip_s on perf_compare, perf_gate and perf_panel leaves out the first seconds (start-up) of each run; perf_history follows FPS, hitches and memory across runs with one name prefix, oldest first; perf_gate says whether a run meets budgets you set (FPS floor, hitch or memory ceiling); perf_panel writes an HTML page to look at one or two runs in a browser. trace_tables and trace_query need the .trace, kept only with KEEP_TRACE=1. When perf_record ends it stops every program of its Wine prefix, or every process named like a native program. To compare native Metal with a translation layer without a game of one's own: workload_list, workload_fetch, then perf_record with workload and api (and example, for a workload that lists examples), or the compare-layer prompt. perf_sweep records one run per value of dim, example, api or an environment variable and fits GPU ms per frame on the value. memory_free_pct holds the whole Mac short of memory while recording (keep other work off it) and background throttles the program: repeat a run that uses either.

tools.description:
Records `program` (an .exe under Wine, or a macOS binary with wine="native"), or a test program fetched with
workload_fetch (workload, api, dim), for `seconds` with Metal System Trace and returns its summary: GPU ms per
frame, frame intervals, FPS, Metal and resident memory (memory=false skips the Metal memory table, the slowest
to read). When it ends it stops every program of that Wine prefix (wineserver -k), or every process named like
the program with native. counters=true also records Metal GPU Counters (`gpu_counters` in the summary: the units the
GPU waited on, its utilization, occupancy and memory bandwidth); it adds about 40 s of read-back per recorded second.

tools.name: perf_runs
tools.title: List recordings

tools.description:
Compares two saved recordings (names from perf_runs), a the reference and b the run after a change: the
headline numbers (FPS, GPU ms, frame pacing, memory), then what changed in the GPU work and where: encoders and
command buffers per frame, the share of encoders under short_us, the GPU's idle time, and each encoder label's
count and GPU ms per frame, largest change first. layer says whether both ran on the same translation layer:
with different layers it compares layers, not one change. A Windows run against a Metal run has `measure`: the
GPU ms and Metal memory differ in kind and the encoders exist only in Metal, so use FPS, its lows, stutter and
jitter. Recordings with under 100 frames are flagged: too short to compare. With markdown true the result also has
`markdown`: the same numbers as tables for a PR comment. skip_s leaves out the first seconds of each recording,
where shaders compile and resources load: the GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed from the
per-frame files without them, and `skipped_s` says it; thermal state, process memory and encoders stay whole-run.
`screen` appears when one run was recorded with the screen locked and the other not: FPS is then not comparable.

a.description: run name from perf_runs: the reference, such as the run before a change

b.description: run name from perf_runs: the run to compare against a

markdown.description: also return the numbers as Markdown tables, default false

short_us.description: an encoder under this GPU time counts as short: 10, 25 (default), 50, 100, 250, 500 or 1000

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them

tools.name: perf_compare
tools.title: Compare two recordings

tools.description:
Names a reference for perf_check, or lists them. With name and runs (names from perf_runs, several runs of the
same program recorded with no change between them), it saves copies of their summaries as the reference `name`,
replacing a previous one, and returns the range each number spans across them: that range, not one run, is what
perf_check judges against, since repeated runs differ by a few percent, and `spread_pct`, each range's width in %
of its midpoint: the noise of this program on this machine, which a change must exceed. With name alone it shows that reference;
with nothing it lists them. With skip_s the reference keeps each run without its first skip_s seconds (the
start-up, as perf_compare's skip_s) and perf_check applies the same cut to the run it judges, so both are
steady-state; the runs need their per-frame files for that.

name.description: reference name: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'; alone, shows that reference

runs.description: run names from perf_runs to save as this reference, ideally 3 or more equal runs; replaces a previous one

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them; perf_check applies the same cut to the run it judges

tools.name: perf_baseline
tools.title: Name a reference

annotations.title: Check a run against a reference

tools.description:
Judges a recording against a reference saved with perf_baseline: regressed when FPS falls under the
reference's lowest FPS by more than margin_pct, GPU ms per frame rises over its highest by more than margin_pct,
or encoders or command buffers per frame exceed its highest; improved when a number leaves the range the other
way and none regressed; same otherwise. Frame pacing, short encoders and GPU idle time are reported by the
comparison but do not decide: they vary too much between equal runs. A run from Windows against a Metal
reference (or the reverse) is judged on FPS alone. A reference saved with skip_s judges the run without its first
skip_s seconds too (`skipped_s` says so). Returns the reasons and perf_compare's
full comparison against the reference's first run.

margin_pct.description: how far outside the reference's range FPS or GPU ms per frame may fall before counting, default 3

tools.name: perf_check
tools.title: Check a run against a reference

tools.description:
Writes a recording's GPU frames as a Chrome trace file, `<run>.chrome-trace` in the runs directory, that
ui.perfetto.dev and chrome://tracing open: one slice per GPU frame, from its start for its GPU time (the sum of
its encoders' time, so a frame with parallel encoders can show shorter than it took), with the compute, fragment
and vertex split as arguments. Returns the file name and the number of frames.
tools.name: perf_export_trace
tools.title: Export frames to Perfetto

tools.description:
Checks a recording against budgets and says pass or fail: a floor for FPS and the 1% low, a ceiling for the
stutter rate, the p95 GPU ms per frame, the hitch count and the peak Metal MiB. Give at least one. A number the
recording lacks fails its budget (value null): a gate must not pass on missing data, nor on a recording whose
program stopped presenting (`unpresented`). Returns each budget with its
limit, the value and whether it held. Use it as a bar a change must clear, where perf_check judges against equal runs.
skip_s leaves out the first seconds of the recording (the start-up), as perf_compare does.

fps_1pct_low_min.description: the 1% low FPS must be at least this

fps_min.description: the FPS must be at least this

gpu_ms_p95_max.description: the p95 GPU ms per frame at most this

hitches_max.description: the number of hitches at most this

metal_mib_max.description: the peak Metal memory in MiB at most this

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them

stutter_rate_pct_max.description: the share of stutter frames, in %, at most this

tools.name: perf_gate
tools.title: Check a run against budgets

tools.description:
Lists the recordings whose name starts with `prefix`, oldest first, with their FPS, 1% low, GPU ms, stutter,
hitches and peak Metal MiB, and the change from the first to the last: how a number moved over a series of runs, such as
one recording per version of a translation layer. Read a trend as real only when it exceeds the spread_pct that
perf_baseline reports for equal runs. Runs from Windows and Metal in one series are flagged: their GPU ms and
memory do not compare. skip_s leaves out the first seconds of each recording (the start-up), as perf_compare does.

prefix.description: the start of the run names to follow: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them

tools.name: perf_history
tools.title: Follow a number across runs

tools.description:
Writes one HTML file, `<name>.panel.html` in the runs directory, that shows one or two recordings in a
browser without a server: GPU time per frame with the hitches marked, the numbers (FPS and its lows, frame
time, jitter, stutter, memory, thermal state), Metal memory over time and, for two runs, A against B. The file
holds the data itself, no path, and loads nothing from the network; the viewer can hide and reorder the
widgets and export the layout as JSON. preset `fps` is the timeline, numbers and memory; `compare` (two runs)
puts A against B first. skip_s leaves out the first seconds of each recording (the start-up), as perf_compare does.
layout (tab ids in the order to show) is saved as panel.json in the runs directory and becomes the default tab
order of every panel, the live one too, until the viewer changes it in the browser; ids left out are hidden but
can be switched back on; tabs are tests (each run against the project's reference), summary, ab, frames, encoders, counters,
memory and data (a panel.json that does not name tests shows it first; one that leaves out any other keeps it hidden),
and a panel.json you wrote yourself, or copied from the panel's Layout JSON, works the same.
Returns the file name, the runs, the frames shown and the file's bytes.

layout.description: tabs to show, in order: tests, summary, ab, frames, encoders, counters, memory, data; saved as panel.json in the runs directory as the default for every panel

name.description: name for the panel file: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'

runs.description: one or two run names from perf_runs; with two, the first is A, the reference

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start of each recording, where shaders compile and resources load; 0 (default) keeps all. The GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them

tools.name: perf_panel
tools.title: Write an HTML panel

tools.description:
Says whether a saved recording splits its GPU work into too many short encoders, the pattern of translation
layers such as DXMT, Mullion or MoltenVK, with the numbers behind it: encoders and command buffers per frame, the
share of short encoders, the labels with the most GPU time and the GPU's idle time. Read the idle time together
with the FPS: a program waiting for vsync idles too. Defaults come from bgfx 17-drawstress on an M1 Pro: 7
encoders per frame and 50% under 25 us under Mullion, 2 and 2% in native Metal.

min_encoders.description: encoders per frame (median) from which the verdict can be yes, default 4

short_share.description: share of short encoders from which the verdict is yes, default 0.25

short_us.description: an encoder under this GPU time counts as short: 10, 25 (default), 50, 100, 250, 500 or 1000

tools.name: perf_diagnose
tools.title: Diagnose encoder use

tools.description: Lists the data tables (schemas) a .trace recording holds; recordings keep their .trace only with KEEP_TRACE=1.

trace.description: a run name from perf_runs whose trace_kept is true, or the path of a .trace

tools.name: trace_tables
tools.title: List a trace's tables

tools.description:
Counts the rows of several tables of a kept .trace, in all and per process, so a recording's useful tables
show before reading them: a table with 0 rows needs another instrument or Xcode, not a bigger page.

tables.description: table names from trace_tables; default the tables that matter for a translation layer

trace.description: a run name from perf_runs whose trace_kept is true, or the path of a .trace

tools.name: trace_count
tools.title: Count a trace's rows

tools.description: Returns one page of rows of one table of a .trace as {column: value}, optionally only one process's rows.

limit.description: rows per page, default 50, at most 500

schema.description: a table name that trace_tables lists, such as metal-gpu-intervals

trace.description: a run name from perf_runs whose trace_kept is true, or the path of a .trace

tools.name: trace_query
tools.title: Read a trace table

tools.description:
Reads a Metal .gputrace capture without Xcode: command buffers, encoders, draws, debug groups, and the 100
most frequent call ids out of calls_total.

capture.description: path of a .gputrace bundle saved from Xcode, inside METAL_TRACE_OUT or METAL_TRACE_READ

tools.name: capture_summary
tools.title: Summarize a capture

tools.description: Returns one page of the records of a .gputrace command stream, with their Metal call names when known.

capture.description: path of a .gputrace bundle saved from Xcode, inside METAL_TRACE_OUT or METAL_TRACE_READ

limit.description: rows per page, default 50, at most 500

tools.name: capture_records
tools.title: Read a capture's records

tools.description:
Apple's published facts for one GPU family, by family ("Apple7") or chip ("M1 Pro"): its chips, what it adds,
its limits, plus the limits shared by all families and the footnotes. Source URLs are in the result.

name.description: a family (Apple7 to Apple10) or a chip (M1 Pro, M2, M4 Max, A17 Pro)

tools.name: gpu_family
tools.title: Apple GPU family facts

tools.description:
Lists the test programs workload_fetch can download, such as bgfx's drawstress: what each measures, its size,
license and APIs, and whether it is already downloaded.
tools.name: workload_list
tools.title: List test programs

tools.description:
Downloads a test program from this project's GitHub releases once, checks its SHA-256 against the one this
package pins, and keeps it in ~/Library/Caches/metal-gpu-trace; later calls reuse it. The programs are built
from source by the project's workloads workflow. A workload with `downloads` (Godot) also fetches each of those
zip files from its own publisher, checks its SHA-512 against the one data/workloads.json pins and unzips it into
the workload's folder.

name.description: a workload name from workload_list, such as drawstress

tools.name: workload_fetch
tools.title: Download a test program

tools.description:
Windows only: downloads Intel's PresentMon console application (MIT) from its GitHub release, checks its
SHA-256 against the one this package pins, and keeps it in %LOCALAPPDATA%\metal-gpu-trace, where perf_record and
perf_attach find it; later calls reuse it. It needs administrator rights or the Performance Log Users group to run.
tools.name: presentmon_install
tools.title: Install PresentMon (Windows)
